notes:
SUMMARY: LumenFlow builds an IDE copilot embedded in their Electron-based IDE. Primary ask: sub-50ms TTFT for single-line completions and deterministic jitter profile for streaming token deltas. Strong interest in token budget tuning (client-side and server-side), model pinning per-route, and graceful fallback to smaller models for quick suggestions.

RECENT TIMELINE:
- 2026-02-12: Intro call (AE Maya) — described product, latency constraints, initial cost targets.
- 2026-02-20: Tech deep-dive with SE Diego — discussed streaming wire protocol, chunk sizes, websocket backpressure patterns. Fireflies ff-20260302-9842.
- 2026-03-02: Internal infra review started (security). Sent security questionnaire (SEC-1187).
- 2026-03-09: Demo w/ hosted API showing streaming prototype (40–70ms TTFT median on small sample). Recorded ff-20260309-1098.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS / NOTES:
- TTFT target: <= 40ms median for single-line completions (40–60 token outputs), p95 < 120ms. Jitter requirement: < 10ms standard deviation for token emission intervals to keep caret movement smooth.
- Throughput: Concurrent 400 active dev sessions during peak (burst to 800). Typical completion length 30–150 tokens.
- Token budget tuning: Need server-side configurable per-route token caps + client hints (preferred max_tokens, soft budget vs hard stop). Want dynamic budgets: e.g., quick-suggestion path (max 40 tokens, high-priority low-latency) and deep-completion path (max 250 tokens, allow batching).
- Streaming: Expect delta-streaming of token chunks every 8–12ms ideally; comfortable with 20ms if deterministic. Need support for TLS websockets and HTTP/2 streaming.
- Backpressure: Client must be able to signal backpressure; prefer server-side continuous batching but must preserve low-latency SLO for critical route. Ask: how Redwood handles request queuing vs immediate fallback to pinned smaller model.
- Model/version pinning: Pin per-route stable model (e.g., model-x-3b-q8) with automated canary rollout. Want simple API to pin and rollback without code changes.
- Caching: LumenFlow will use prefix/KV caching for repeated snippets; needs TTL controls and token-accounting for cache hits.
- Cost sensitivity: Moderate; open to dedicated capacity if cost and latency predictable. Interested in Optimize recommendations for quantization profiles to hit TTFT.

POC PLAN (requested):
- 2-week POC: 1) run streaming benchmark harness with Redwood hosted API; 2) enable token-budget per-route and measure policy effects; 3) test fallback path (model A -> model B) under simulated overload; 4) collect per-token latency traces.
- Success criteria: median TTFT <= 40ms on 80% of dev sessions; p95 token emission jitter < 10ms; fallback mean latency < 80ms.

QUOTES / CALL NOTES:
- "We need the IDE to feel like typing — if tokens pop late or jittered, devs lose flow." — Lead PM (call).
- AE notes: client debounce + prefetch heuristics may mitigate some SLO breaches; still require server guarantees for critical route.

NEXT STEPS / ACTION ITEMS:

- LumenFlow to complete security questionnaire and share on-prem compatibility matrix.
- Schedule POC kickoff (target week of 2026-03-22).
